title: A note scribbled in a book’s margin took 358 years to prove
body: Around 1637, Pierre de Fermat wrote in his copy of the ancient Greek text Arithmetica that a^n + b^n = c^n has no solutions in positive whole numbers when n is greater than 2. He added that he had a truly marvellous proof the margin was too narrow to contain. Generations of mathematicians failed to find one, until Andrew Wiles proved it in 1994 using advanced 20th-century tools, which is why most experts doubt Fermat ever had a valid proof.

slides.question: Why do most experts doubt that Fermat really had a proof?
options: The margin note was a later forgery
Fermat admitted it in a later letter
slides.explanation: Generations of mathematicians failed, and Andrew Wiles’s 1994 proof relies on advanced 20th-century mathematics, so most experts doubt Fermat ever had a valid proof.
